sentences.zh: 載記序

translations.literal: Preface to the Records.
translations.idiomatic: Preface to the *Zaiji* annals.

sentences.zh: 古者帝王，乃生奇類、淳維，伯禹之苗裔，豈異類哉？

translations.literal: Of old the August Lords and Kings gave birth to strange stocks such as Chunwei, lineal descendants of Lord Yu—how could they be a different kind?
translations.idiomatic: Ancient emperors counted even alien lines like Chunwei among the descendants of Great Yu—hardly a separate species.

sentences.zh: 反首衣皮，餐膻飲湩，而震驚中域，其來自遠。

translations.literal: They turned their heads, wore pelts, ate rank flesh and drank curds, yet shook the central domains; their coming lay far in the past.
translations.idiomatic: They wore furs, ate mutton, drank kumiss, yet convulsed the heartland—their roots lay deep in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 天未悔禍，種落彌繁。

translations.literal: Heaven had not yet repented the disaster, and their tribes grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had not yet called off the scourge, and their clans multiplied.

sentences.zh: 其風俗險詖，性靈馳突，前史載之，亦以詳備。

translations.literal: Their customs were crafty and crooked, their temperaments headstrong; earlier histories recorded them in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: Their ways were sly and abrupt, their natures fierce—earlier histories already told the tale in exhaustive detail.

sentences.zh: 軒帝患其干紀，所以徂征；

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor worried that they would violate the norm, and therefore marched against them;
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor feared they would break the cosmic order and campaigned against them;

sentences.zh: 武王竄以荒服，同乎禽獸。

translations.literal: King Wu banished them to the wild outer zone, treating them like birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu pushed them into the outermost wilds, no better than beasts in policy.

sentences.zh: 而於露寒之野，候月覘風，睹隙揚埃，乘間騁暴，邊城不得緩帶，百姓靡有室家。

translations.literal: Yet on the steppes of dew and cold they watched the moon and spied the wind, seized gaps and raised dust, exploited openings to run riot; border cities could not loosen their belts, and commoners had no homes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet on the open steppe they watched seasons and winds, struck whenever a crack appeared, and raided at will—so frontier garrisons never rested and the people lost hearth and home.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「微管仲，吾其被髮左衽矣。

translations.literal: Confucius said, "Without Guan Zhong, I would let my hair down and button my robe on the left."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Without Guan Zhong we should all have gone unbound-haired with robes buttoned left—barbarians."

sentences.zh: 」此言能教訓卒伍，整齊車甲，邊埸既伏，境內以安。

translations.literal: This speaks of one who could drill the ranks, align chariots and armour, so that the border submitted and the interior was calm.
translations.idiomatic: He meant a minister who could train troops, fit out armies, quiet the frontier, and secure the interior.

sentences.zh: 然則燕築造陽之郊，秦塹臨洮之險，登天山，絕地脈，苞玄菟，款黃河，所以防夷狄之亂中華，其備豫如此。

translations.literal: Thus Yan built walls at Zaoyang's outskirts, Qin trenched the peril of Lintao, ascended Heaven Mountain, cut the earth's veins, embraced Xuandu, and bowed to the Yellow River—all to guard the Hua heartland from the Di and Yi, with precautions so thorough.
translations.idiomatic: So Yan walled Zaoyang, Qin ditched Lintao, climbed the Heavenly Mountain, choked the passes, wrapped Xuandu, and bent the Yellow River into a shield—every device to keep the barbarians from China.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝初納呼韓，居之亭鄣，委以候望，始寬戎狄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han Xuandi he admitted Huhanye, housed him in signal towers and stockades, entrusted him with watch duties, and first relaxed control over the Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xuandi first admitted Huhanye, lodged him inside the beacon line, and gave him scout duty—opening the door to the steppe peoples.

sentences.zh: 光武亦以南庭數萬徙入西河，後亦轉至五原，連延七郡。

translations.literal: Guangwu also moved several tens of thousands of the southern court into Xihe, later shifted them to Wuyuan, stretching across seven commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu likewise resettled tens of thousands of southern Xiongnu into Xihe, later spreading them through Wuyuan across seven commanderies.

sentences.zh: 董卓之亂，則汾晉之郊蕭然矣。

translations.literal: At the turmoil of Dong Zhuo, then the Fen and Jin hinterlands were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo wrecked the capital, the Fen and Jin borderlands were stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 郭欽騰箋于武帝，江統獻策于惠皇，皆以為魏處戎夷，繡居都鄙，請移沙塞之表，定一殷周之服。

translations.literal: Guo Qin sent a memorial soaring to Emperor Wu, and Jiang Tong offered strategy to Emperor Hui; both held that Wei had quartered Rong and Yi embroidered among capital and district, and requested moving them beyond the sandy wastes to fix the single garment-zone of Yin and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Qin petitioned Emperor Wu and Jiang Tong briefed Emperor Hui, both arguing that Wei had lodged barbarians inside the inner districts and urging their removal beyond the deserts to restore the classical inner-outer divide.

sentences.zh: 統則憂諸並部，欽則慮在盟津。

translations.literal: Tong worried about the Bing provinces together; Qin fretted over the Meng ford.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tong feared the clustered Bing garrisons; Guo Qin eyed the Mengjin crossing.

sentences.zh: 言猶自口，元海已至。

translations.literal: The words were still in their mouths, yet Yuanhai had already arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Their warnings were barely spoken when Liu Yuan was already at the gates.

sentences.zh: 語曰「失以豪厘」，晉卿大夫之辱也。

translations.literal: The saying runs, 'Loss begins from a hair's breadth'—it is the shame of Jin's ministers and grandees.
translations.idiomatic: The proverb says error starts at a hairline—Jin's great officers earned that reproach.

sentences.zh: 聰之誓兵，東兼齊地；

translations.literal: When Cong swore in the troops, he annexed the Qi lands eastward;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Cong mobilized eastward he swallowed the old Qi domain;

sentences.zh: 曜之馳旆，西逾隴山，覆沒兩京，蒸徒百萬。

translations.literal: when Yao flew his banners, he crossed Long Mountain westward, overthrew the two capitals, and steamed a million thralls.
translations.idiomatic: when Liu Yao drove west past Longshan, he toppled both capitals and trampled a million subjects.

sentences.zh: 天子陵江禦物，分據地險，回首中原，力不能救，劃長淮以北，大抵棄之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven crossed the Yangzi to stem the flood, split and held perilous ground, turned his head toward the central plain yet lacked strength to save it, and north of the long Huai was largely abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled across the Yangzi to stem the tide, clung to river defences, gazed back at the north he could not save, and yielded everything north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 胡人利我艱虞，分鑣起亂；

translations.literal: The Hu profited from our distress and raised rebellion on every road;
translations.idiomatic: The steppe peoples seized on Jin's distress and rose in every quarter;

sentences.zh: 晉臣或阻兵遐遠，接武效尤。

translations.literal: Jin ministers too blocked troops in distant corners and followed suit one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Jin commanders likewise froze armies far away and copied their treason.

sentences.zh: 大凡劉元海以惠帝永興元年據離石稱漢。

translations.literal: In general Liu Yuanhai in the first year of Yongxing of Emperor Hui occupied Lishi and styled his state Han.
translations.idiomatic: In sum Liu Yuan in Emperor Hui's Yongxing year one seized Lishi and proclaimed Han.

sentences.zh: 後九年，石勒據襄國稱趙。

translations.literal: Nine years later Shi Le occupied Xiangguo and styled Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years on Shi Le took Xiangguo and called his state Zhao.

sentences.zh: 張氏先據河西，是歲，自石勒後三十六年也，重華自稱涼王。

translations.literal: The Zhang house had first held Hexi; in that year—thirty-six years after Shi Le—Chonghua styled himself Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang clan already held Hexi; thirty-six years after Shi Le, Zhang Chonghua declared himself Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 後一年，冉閔據鄴稱魏。

translations.literal: One year later Ran Min held Ye and styled Wei.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Ran Min seized Ye as Wei.

sentences.zh: 後一年，苻健據長安稱秦。

translations.literal: One year later Fu Jian held Chang'an as Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Another year and Fu Jian took Chang'an as Qin.

sentences.zh: 慕容氏先據遼東稱燕，是歲，自苻健後一年也，俊始僭號。

translations.literal: The Murong house had first held Liaodong as Yan; in that year—one year after Fu Jian—Jun first usurped the title.
translations.idiomatic: Murong had long ruled Yan in Liaodong; the year after Fu Jian, Murong Jun claimed the imperial style.

sentences.zh: 後三十一年，後燕慕容垂據鄴。

translations.literal: Thirty-one years later Later Yan's Murong Chui held Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-one years on Murong Chui's Later Yan sat in Ye.

sentences.zh: 後二年，西燕慕容沖據阿房。

translations.literal: Two years later Western Yan's Murong Chong held Epang.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Western Yan's Murong Chong seized Epang.

sentences.zh: 是歲也，乞伏國仁據桴罕稱秦。

translations.literal: In that year Qifu Guoren held Fuhan as Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Qifu Guoren took Fuhan as Qin.

sentences.zh: 後一年，慕容永據上黨。

translations.literal: One year later Murong Yong held Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Murong Yong held Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 是歲也，呂光據姑臧稱涼。

translations.literal: In that year Lü Guang held Guzang as Liang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Lü Guang took Guzang as Liang.

sentences.zh: 後十二年，慕容德據滑台稱南燕。

translations.literal: Twelve years later Murong De held Huatai as Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years on Murong De's Southern Yan ruled Huatai.

sentences.zh: 是歲也，禿髮烏孤據廉川稱南涼，段業據張掖稱北涼。

translations.literal: In that year Tufa Wugu held Lianchuan as Southern Liang, and Duan Ye held Zhangye as Northern Liang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tufa Wugu founded Southern Liang at Lianchuan while Duan Ye's Northern Liang sat at Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 後三年，李玄盛據敦煌稱西涼。

translations.literal: Three years later Li Xisheng held Dunhuang as Western Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Li Gao's Western Liang took Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 後一年，沮渠蒙遜殺段業，自稱涼。

translations.literal: One year later Juqu Mengxun killed Duan Ye and styled himself Liang.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Juqu Mengxun slew Duan Ye and claimed Liang.

sentences.zh: 後四年，譙縱據蜀稱成都王。

translations.literal: Four years later Qiao Zong held Shu as Prince of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later Qiao Zong carved out Chengdu in Shu.

sentences.zh: 後二年，赫連勃勃據朔方稱大夏。

translations.literal: Two years later Helian Bobo held Shuofang as Great Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on Helian Bobo styled Great Xia from Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 後二年，馮跋殺離班，據和龍稱北燕。

translations.literal: Two years later Feng Ba slew Li Ban and held Helong as Northern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Feng Ba killed Li Ban and ruled Northern Yan from Helong.

sentences.zh: 提封天下，十喪其八，莫不龍旌帝服，建社開祊，華夷咸暨，人物斯在。

translations.literal: Measured across the realm, eight tenths were lost; none failed to fly dragon banners and don imperial robes, raise altars and open ancestral shrines—barbarian and Han alike—yet the actors all stood there.
translations.idiomatic: Eight parts in ten of the map were gone; every warlord, Hu or Han, hoisted dragon standards, donned imperial dress, founded shrines, and claimed the mandate.

sentences.zh: 或篡通都之鄉，或擁數州之地，雄圖內卷，師旅外並，窮兵凶於勝負，盡人命於鋒鏑，其為戰國者一百三十六載，抑元海為之禍首云。

translations.literal: Some usurped the heart of a great metropolis, some hugged several provinces; grand designs curled inward while armies clashed without; they exhausted the people on spearpoints for a hundred thirty-six years of warring states—Yuanhai, it is said, was the chief author of the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Some seized the capital belt, others clutched whole regions; ambition turned inward while armies devoured one another for one hundred thirty-six years of ceaseless war—and Liu Yuan is named the spark that lit it all.

sentences.zh: 劉元海

translations.literal: Liu Yuanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanhai.

sentences.zh: 劉元海，新興匈奴人，冒頓之後也。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanhai was a Xiongnu of Xinxing, a descendant of Modu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan was a Xiongnu from Xinxing, descended from Modun Shanyu.

sentences.zh: 名犯高祖廟諱

translations.literal: His given name infringed the temple taboo on Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: His personal name violated the high temple taboo on Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 〈名淵，與唐高祖同名〉

translations.literal: (His name was Yuan, the same as Tang Gaozu's name.)
translations.idiomatic: The commentary notes his registered name was Yuan, identical to Tang Gaozu's.

sentences.zh: ，故稱其字焉。

translations.literal: , therefore they call him by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the history uses his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 初，漢高祖以宗女為公主，以妻冒頓，約為兄弟，故其子孫遂冒姓劉氏。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Gaozu took an imperial clanswoman as princess and gave her in marriage to Modu, covenanting as brothers; therefore his descendants took the surname Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu married a house princess to Modu as brother sovereigns, so the chanyu's house adopted the Liu surname.

sentences.zh: 建武初，烏珠留若鞮單于子右奧鞬日逐王比自立為南單于，入居西河美稷，今離石左國城即單于所徙庭也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, the son of Wuzhiliu Ruoti Shanyu, the Right Worthy King of the Gullet Sun, Bi, set himself up as southern Shanyu and entered to dwell at Meiji in Xihe; today's Zuoguocheng of Lishi is the court to which the Shanyu moved.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu the Right Gullet King Bi, son of Wuzhiliu Ruoti, declared himself southern Shanyu and moved his court to Meiji in Xihe—modern Zuoguocheng beside Lishi.

sentences.zh: 中平中，單于羌渠使子於扶羅將兵助漢，討平黃巾。

translations.literal: In the Zhongping era Shanyu Qiangqu sent his son Yuluoji with troops to aid Han and help pacify the Yellow Turbans.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhongping Shanyu Qiangqu sent Yuluoji to help Han crush the Yellow Turbans.

sentences.zh: 會羌渠為國人所殺，於扶羅以其眾留漢，自立為單于。

translations.literal: When Qiangqu was killed by his countrymen, Yuluoji kept his host in Han lands and set himself up as Shanyu.
translations.idiomatic: When clansmen murdered Qiangqu, Yuluoji stayed in China and proclaimed himself Shanyu.

sentences.zh: 屬董卓之亂，寇掠太原、河東，屯於河內。

translations.literal: At the time of Dong Zhuo's turmoil they raided Taiyuan and Hedong and camped in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Amid Dong Zhuo's chaos they plundered Taiyuan and Hedong and encamped in Henei.

sentences.zh: 於扶羅死，弟呼廚泉立，以於扶羅子豹為左賢王，即元海之父也。

translations.literal: When Yuluoji died, his younger brother Huchuquan succeeded, appointing Yuluoji's son Bao as Left Worthy King—he was Yuanhai's father.
translations.idiomatic: Yuluoji's brother Huchuquan succeeded and named Yuluoji's son Liu Bao left worthy king—Liu Yuan's father.

sentences.zh: 魏武分其眾為五部，以豹為左部帥，其餘部帥皆以劉氏為之。

translations.literal: Wei Wu divided their host into five divisions, making Bao commander of the left division; the other division commanders were all Liu clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao split the horde into five sections with Liu Bao heading the left; every other section chief was also a Liu.

sentences.zh: 太康中，改置都尉，左部居太原茲氏，右部居祁，南部居蒲子，北部居新興，中部居大陵。

translations.literal: In the Taikang era they were reorganized as commandants; the left section dwelt at Zishi in Taiyuan, the right at Qi, the south at Puzi, the north at Xinxing, and the center at Daling.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taikang they were retitled commandants: left at Zishi in Taiyuan, right at Qi, south at Puzi, north at Xinxing, center at Daling.

sentences.zh: 劉氏雖分居五部，然皆居於晉陽汾澗之濱。

translations.literal: Though the Liu surname was split among five sections, all dwelt along the Fen and Jian streams below Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Liu clansmen were parceled into five commands, they all lived along the Fen and Jian rivers below Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 豹妻呼延氏，魏嘉平中祈子于龍門，俄而有一大魚，頂有二角，軒鬐躍鱗而至祭所，久之乃去。

translations.literal: Bao's wife the Lady Huyan, in the Wei Jiaping era prayed for a child at Longmen; presently a great fish with two horns on its head, high fins and leaping scales, came to the sacrifice place and after a long while departed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huyan prayed at Longmen during Wei Jiaping; a huge horned fish with towering fins flopped up to the altar and then swam away.

sentences.zh: 巫覡皆異之，曰：「此嘉祥也。

translations.literal: The shamans all marvelled, saying, "This is an auspicious portent."
translations.idiomatic: The shamans cried an omen: "This is heaven-sent good fortune."

sentences.zh: 」其夜夢旦所見魚變為人，左手把一物，大如半雞子，光景非常，授呼延氏，曰：「此是日精，服之生貴子。

translations.literal: That night she dreamed the fish seen at dawn became a man, holding in his left hand an object the size of half a chicken egg, of extraordinary radiance; he gave it to Lady Huyan, saying, "This is the essence of the sun; swallow it and you will bear a noble son."
translations.idiomatic: That night she dreamed the fish turned into a man who pressed into her palm a sun-bright pearl, saying, "Swallow this essence of the day-star and you will bear a lord among men."

sentences.zh: 」寤而告豹，豹曰：「吉徵也。

translations.literal: Awakening she told Bao, who said, "It is a lucky sign.
translations.idiomatic: She woke and told Liu Bao, who said, "Heaven favours us.

sentences.zh: 吾昔從邯鄲張冏母司徒氏相，云吾當有貴子孫，三世必大昌，仿像相符矣。

translations.literal: Long ago the diviner Mother Situ of Handan Zhang Jiong told me I would have noble descendants, and for three generations there would be great flourishing—it seems to match.
translations.idiomatic: Mother Situ of Handan once read my face and promised noble grandsons and three generations of glory—this fits that prophecy.

sentences.zh: 」自是十三月而生元海，左手文有其名，遂以名焉。

translations.literal: From this after thirteen months she bore Yuanhai; on his left hand were characters forming his name, and therefore he was so named.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen months later she bore Liu Yuan; his left palm bore the characters of his name, so they called him Yuan.

sentences.zh: 齠齔英慧，七歲遭母憂，擗踴號叫，哀感旁鄰，宗族部落咸共歎賞。

translations.literal: In childhood he was bright; at seven he met mourning for his mother, beat his breast and wailed until grief touched the neighbours; clan and tribe together sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he showed genius; at seven he mourned his mother with such tearing grief that neighbours wept; kinsmen and tribesmen marvelled.

sentences.zh: 時司空太原王昶聞而嘉之，並遣吊賻。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Works Wang Chang of Taiyuan heard and praised him, and also sent condolences and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Wang Chang of Taiyuan heard the tale, praised the boy, and sent funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，師事上党崔游，習《毛詩》、《京氏易》、《馬氏尚書》，尤好《春秋左氏傳》、《孫吳兵法》，略皆誦之，《史》、《漢》、諸子，無不綜覽。

translations.literal: In youth he loved study, took as teacher Cui You of Shangdang, studied Mao's Odes, Jing's Changes, Ma's Documents, and especially loved Zuo's Tradition of the Spring and Autumn and the Sun and Wu Art of War—he could recite them all in outline—and comprehensively surveyed the Records, Han, and the masters.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books early, studied under Cui You of Shangdang, mastered the Mao Odes, Jing Changes, Ma Rong's Documents, devoured Zuo's *Spring and Autumn* commentary and the Sunzi-Wuzi military classics, and read widely in the histories and philosophers.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂同門生硃紀、範隆曰：「吾每觀書傳，常鄙隨陸無武，降灌無文。

translations.literal: Once he said to fellow students Zhu Ji and Fan Long, "Whenever I read histories I always despise Sui He and Lu Jia for lacking martial prowess, and Zhou Bo and Guan Ying for lacking literary polish.
translations.idiomatic: He once told Zhu Ji and Fan Long, "Reading history I always scoff that Sui He and Lu Jia had no sword, while Zhou Bo and Guan Ying had no brush.

sentences.zh: 道由人弘，一物之不知者，固君子之所恥也。

translations.literal: The Way is enlarged by men; not to know a single thing is indeed what a gentleman should be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: The Way spreads through human effort; ignorance of even one art is a gentleman's shame.

sentences.zh: 二生遇高皇而不能建封侯之業，兩公屬太宗而不能開庠序之美，惜哉！

translations.literal: The two students met the High Founder yet could not build a marquis's achievement; the two dukes served the Founding Ancestor yet could not open the beauty of schools—how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Those worthies served Han's founder yet never matched his martial glory, and aided Wenjing yet never spread culture—what a waste!

sentences.zh: 」於是遂學武事，妙絕於眾，猿臂善射，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he studied military affairs, was wondrously supreme among the host, had ape arms and excelled at archery, and his strength surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: So he drilled in arms, outshone every comrade, shot like Yi, and wielded strength beyond mortal measure.

sentences.zh: 姿儀魁偉，身長八尺四寸，須長三尺餘，當心有赤毫毛三根，長三尺六寸。

translations.literal: His bearing was lofty and grand; he stood eight chi four cun tall, his beard over three chi long, and on his breast were three red down hairs three chi six cun long.
translations.idiomatic: He was a giant of eight feet four inches with a three-foot beard and three crimson hairs three feet six inches long on his breast.

sentences.zh: 有屯留崔懿之、襄陵公師彧等，皆善相人，及見元海，驚而相謂曰：「此人形貌非常，吾所未見也。

translations.literal: There were Cui Yizhi of Tunliu, Gongshi Yu of Xiangling, and others, all skilled at physiognomy; when they saw Yuanhai they started and said to each other, "This man's form and bearing are extraordinary—we have never seen the like."
translations.idiomatic: Physiognomists such as Cui Yizhi and Gongshi Yu gasped when they saw him: "We have never read a face like his."

sentences.zh: 」於是深相崇敬，推分結恩。

translations.literal: Thereupon they deeply revered him, sharing portions and knotting kindness.
translations.idiomatic: They pledged him deep respect, broke bread with him, and swore friendship.

sentences.zh: 太原王渾虛襟友之，命子濟拜焉。

translations.literal: Wang Hun of Taiyuan opened his bosom as friend and ordered his son Ji to bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun of Taiyuan befriended him openly and told his son Wang Ji to treat him as elder.

sentences.zh: 咸熙中，為任子在洛陽，文帝深待之。

translations.literal: In the Xianxi era he was hostage-son in Luoyang, and Emperor Wen treated him with deep favour.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianxi he was a hostage noble in Luoyang, and Sima Zhao favoured him.

sentences.zh: 泰始之後，渾又屢言之于武帝。

translations.literal: After Taishi, Hun again repeatedly spoke of him to Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After Taishi began Wang Hun kept recommending him to Sima Yan.

sentences.zh: 帝召與語，大悅之，謂王濟曰：「劉元海容儀機鑒，雖由餘、日磾無以加也。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him to converse, greatly delighted in him, and said to Wang Ji, "Liu Yuanhai's mien and insight—even You Yu and Jin Midi could not surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor interviewed Liu Yuan and told Wang Ji, "For presence and penetration even Jin Midi and You Yu would not surpass him."

sentences.zh: 」濟對曰：「元海儀容機鑒，實如聖旨，然其文武才幹賢於二子遠矣。

translations.literal: Ji replied, "Yuanhai's bearing and insight are indeed as Your Majesty's edict says, yet his civil and martial talent and capacity surpass those two sons by far.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji answered, "You speak true of his charisma, but his civil and military gifts outstrip those two by far.

sentences.zh: 陛下若任之以東南之事，吳會不足平也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty assigns him southeast affairs, Wu and Yue will not be enough to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Give him the southeast and Wu-Yue would fall in a campaign.

sentences.zh: 」帝稱善。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called it excellent advice.

sentences.zh: 孔恂、楊珧進曰：「臣觀元海之才，當今懼無其比，陛下若輕其眾，不足以成事；

translations.literal: Kong Xun and Yang Yao advanced, saying, "Your servant observes Yuanhai's talent—today there is none to compare; if Your Majesty lightly employs his host, it will not suffice to accomplish the deed;
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xun and Yang Yao objected: "No one today matches Liu Yuan; if you treat his tribes lightly you may fail the mission;

sentences.zh: 若假之威權，平吳之後，恐其不復北渡也。

translations.literal: if you lend him awesome authority, after pacifying Wu I fear he will not again cross northward.
translations.idiomatic: yet arm him with full power and once Wu falls he may never return north.

sentences.zh: 非我族類，其心必異。

translations.literal: Those who are not of our kind are sure to have different hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Alien stock never shares the same heart.

sentences.zh: 任之以本部，臣竊為陛下寒心。

translations.literal: To assign him to his native command—your servant privately chills for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Let him lead his own tribes and I tremble for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 若舉天阻之固以資之，無乃不可乎！

translations.literal: To supply him with the solidity of heaven's barrier—can that be permissible!
translations.idiomatic: Hand him the northern bastions and you arm a dragon—how can that be wise?

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: The Emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent.

sentences.zh: 後秦涼覆沒，帝疇咨將帥，上党李憙曰：「陛下誠能發匈奴五部之眾，假元海一將軍之號，鼓行而西，可指期而定。

translations.literal: Later Qin and Liang were overthrown; the Emperor consulted on commanders, and Li Xi of Shangdang said, "If Your Majesty truly can mobilize the five Xiongnu sections and lend Yuanhai a general's title, beating the drum westward, it can be settled on a set date.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang collapsed the court debated generals; Li Xi of Shangdang said, "Mobilize the five Xiongnu divisions, give Liu Yuan a general's baton, and march west on schedule—the west will fall.

sentences.zh: 」孔恂曰：「李公之言，未盡殄患之理也。

translations.literal: Kong Xun said, "Lord Li's words do not exhaust the principle of exterminating disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xun retorted, "That plan does not finish the danger.

sentences.zh: 」憙勃然曰：「以匈奴之勁悍，元海之曉兵，奉宣聖威，何不盡之有！

translations.literal: Xi flared and said, "With the Xiongnu's fierce strength and Yuanhai's knowledge of arms, carrying out the sage awe—what could not be utterly possessed!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi snapped, "Their ferocity plus Liu Yuan's craft, carrying imperial majesty—what could resist?"

sentences.zh: 」恂曰：「元海若能平涼州，斬樹機能，恐涼州方有難耳。

translations.literal: Xun said, "If Yuanhai can pacify Liangzhou and behead Shu Jinen, I fear Liangzhou will then have disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Kong answered, "Let Liu Yuan take Liangzhou and slay the rebel Shu Jinen and Liangzhou will merely trade one peril for another.

sentences.zh: 蛟龍得雲雨，非復池中物也。

translations.literal: When a flood-dragon gains clouds and rain, it is no longer a creature in the pond.
translations.idiomatic: Give a kraken cloud and rain and it leaves the pool forever.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 後王彌從洛陽東歸，元海餞彌于九曲之濱。

translations.literal: Later Wang Mi returned east from Luoyuan; Yuanhai feasted Mi on the bank of the Jiuqu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mi left Luoyang for the east, Liu Yuan feasted him on the Jiuqu bend.

sentences.zh: 泣謂彌曰：「王渾、李憙以鄉曲見知，每相稱達，讒間因之而進，深非吾願，適足為害。

translations.literal: Weeping, he said to Mi, "Wang Hun and Li Xi, knowing me from the same district, always praised and advanced me; slander therefore advanced in turn—it was deeply not my wish and only sufficient to bring harm.
translations.idiomatic: Through tears he told Wang Mi, "Wang Hun and Li Xi, as fellow northerners, praised me until malice followed—never my wish, only a curse.

sentences.zh: 吾本無宦情，惟足下明之。

translations.literal: I fundamentally lack desire for office—only you understand me.
translations.idiomatic: I never hungered for rank—only you can see that.

sentences.zh: 恐死洛陽，永與子別。

translations.literal: I fear I will die in Luoyang and part from you forever.
translations.idiomatic: I may die in Luoyang and never see you again.

sentences.zh: 」因慷慨歔欷，縱酒長嘯，聲調亮然，坐者為之流涕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was stirred and sighed, poured wine freely and gave a long whistle; the tone was clear and bright, and those seated wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: He grew fierce with wine, whistled long and loud, and every guest wept at the sound.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸時在九曲，比聞而馳遣視之，見元海在焉，言於帝曰：「陛下不除劉元海，臣恐并州不得久寧。

translations.literal: Prince Sima You of Qi was at that time at Jiuqu; when he heard nearby he galloped to send someone to look, and seeing Yuanhai there, said to the Emperor, "If Your Majesty does not remove Liu Yuanhai, your servant fears Bingzhou will not long be tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima You was nearby at Jiuqu; he rode over, found Liu Yuan at the banquet, and warned the emperor, "If you leave Liu Yuan alive, Bingzhou will not stay quiet."

sentences.zh: 」王渾進曰：「元海長者，渾為君王保明之。

translations.literal: Wang Hun advanced, saying, "Yuanhai is an elder; Hun for the prince-king vouches for him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hun cut in: "Liu Yuan is a man of honour—I will answer for him before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 且大晉方表信殊俗，懷遠以德，如之何以無萌之疑殺人侍子，以示晉德不弘。

translations.literal: Moreover Great Jin is just now displaying trust toward alien customs, cherishing the distant by virtue—how can we, on suspicion without sprout, kill a man's attendant-son and thereby show that Jin's virtue is not broad.
translations.idiomatic: The court is trying to win the frontier by trust; killing a blameless hostage on a whim would prove our virtue is narrow.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「渾言是也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Hun's words are right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wang Hun is correct."

sentences.zh: 會豹卒，以元海代為左部帥。

translations.literal: When Bao died, Yuanhai was appointed in his stead as commander of the left section.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bao died Liu Yuan succeeded him as left-section chief.

sentences.zh: 太康末，拜北部都尉。

translations.literal: At the end of Taikang he was appointed northern commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taikang he became northern commandant.

sentences.zh: 明刑法，禁奸邪，輕財好施，推誠接物，五部俊傑無不至者。

translations.literal: He clarified penal law, prohibited wickedness, was light with wealth and fond of giving, extended sincerity in receiving people, and there was no outstanding man of the five sections who did not come.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the code, crushed crime, spent freely, dealt honestly, and every notable of the five Xiongnu hosts rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 幽冀名儒，後門秀士，不遠千里，亦皆遊焉。

translations.literal: Famous Ru of You and Ji, talented men from rear gates, not shying a thousand li, all also came to study with him.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian stars from You and Ji and poor scholars crossed a thousand li to sit at his feet.

sentences.zh: 楊駿輔政，以元海為建威將軍、五部大都督，封漢光鄉侯。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun assisted the government, he made Yuanhai General Who Establishes Might, grand commander of the five sections, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Han'guang village.
translations.idiomatic: Regent Yang Jun named him General Who Establishes Might, commander-in-chief of the five sections, and marquis of Hanguang township.

sentences.zh: 元康末，坐部人叛出塞免官。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuankang he lost office because his tribesmen rebelled and fled beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang's end saw him cashiered when his tribesmen broke for the steppe.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎鎮鄴，表元海行甯朔將軍、監五部軍事。

translations.literal: Prince Cheng of Lu, Sima Ying, garrisoned Ye and memorialized Yuanhai as acting General Who Pacifies the North, supervising military affairs of the five sections.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying of Chengdu, stationed at Ye, got him posted acting General Who Pacifies the North over the five sections.

sentences.zh: 惠帝失馭，寇盜蜂起，元海從祖故北部都尉、左賢王劉宣等竊議曰：「昔我先人與漢約為兄弟，憂泰同之。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui lost the reins; bandits sprang like wasps; Yuanhai's granduncle, the former northern commandant and Left Worthy King Liu Xuan, and others secretly deliberated, saying, "Formerly our forefathers covenanted with Han as brothers, sharing joy and peril alike.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Hui lost control, Liu Xuan, former northern commandant and left worthy king, whispered with kinsmen: "Our ancestors swore brotherhood with Han and shared its fate.

sentences.zh: 自漢亡以來，魏晉代興，我單于雖有虛號，無復尺土之業，自諸王侯，降同編戶。

translations.literal: Since Han fell, Wei and Jin rose in turn; our Shanyu, though he kept an empty title, no longer had an enterprise of a foot of soil; from the various princes and marquises downward he was reduced to the same as registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han fell we have kept a hollow title while every prince sank to commoner status on Jin registers.

sentences.zh: 今司馬氏骨肉相殘，四海鼎沸，興邦復業，此其時矣。

translations.literal: Now the Sima clan flesh and blood devour one another and the four seas boil; to raise a state and restore an enterprise—this is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Simas tear one another apart while the realm boils—this is the moment to refound our line.

sentences.zh: 左賢王元海姿器絕人，幹宇超世。

translations.literal: Left Worthy King Yuanhai's mien and capacity surpass others, and his stem and canopy transcend the age.
translations.idiomatic: Left Worthy King Liu Yuan's presence and scope outshine every man of his day.

sentences.zh: 天若不恢崇單于，終不虛生此人也。

translations.literal: If Heaven does not intend to exalt the Shanyu, in the end it would not vainly have born this man.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven would not have bred such a man unless it meant to exalt our Shanyu again.

sentences.zh: 」於是密共推元海為大單于。

translations.literal: Thereupon they secretly together pushed Yuanhai as great Shanyu.
translations.idiomatic: They secretly elected Liu Yuan great Shanyu.

sentences.zh: 乃使其党呼延攸詣鄴，以謀告之。

translations.literal: They then sent their partisan Huyan You to Ye to report the plot to him.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Huyan You to Ye with the plan.

sentences.zh: 元海請歸會葬，穎弗許。

translations.literal: Yuanhai requested leave to return for a funeral assembly; Ying did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan begged leave to mourn; Sima Ying refused.

sentences.zh: 乃令攸先歸，告宣等招集五部，引會宜陽諸胡，聲言應穎，實背之也。

translations.literal: They then ordered You to return first, telling Xuan and the others to gather the five sections and muster the various Hu at Yiyang, declaring they would answer Ying, but in truth betrayed him.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan You raced home to rally the five sections and Yiyang Hu, claiming they would help Sima Ying while plotting the opposite.

sentences.zh: 穎為皇太弟，以元海為太弟屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: When Ying became imperial younger brother, he made Yuanhai Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry of the imperial younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Ying became crown younger brother, Liu Yuan became his garrison-cavalry colonel.

sentences.zh: 惠帝伐穎，次於蕩陰，穎假元海輔國將軍、督北城守事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui attacked Ying and halted at Dangyin, Ying made Yuanhai acting General Who Supports the State and supervised defence of the north wall.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Hui's march on Dangyin, Sima Ying put Liu Yuan in charge of the northern wall.

sentences.zh: 及六軍敗績，穎以元海為冠軍將軍，封盧奴伯。

translations.literal: When the six armies were routed, Ying made Yuanhai General Who Crowns the Army and enfeoffed him as Baron of Lunu.
translations.idiomatic: After the six armies collapsed Sima Ying named him General Who Crowns the Army and baron of Lunu.

sentences.zh: 并州刺史東嬴公騰、安北將軍王浚，起兵伐穎，元海說穎曰：「今二鎮跋扈，眾餘十萬，恐非宿衛及近都士庶所能禦之，請為殿下還說五部，以赴國難。

translations.literal: Governor of Bing Sima Teng of Dongying and General Who Guards the North Wang Jun raised troops to attack Ying; Yuanhai counselled Ying, saying, "Now the two garrisons are overbearing; their hosts exceed a hundred thousand—I fear neither the palace guard nor the gentry near the capital can withstand them; I beg leave for Your Highness to return and persuade the five sections to answer the state's disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou governor Sima Teng and Wang Jun marched on Ye with a hundred thousand men; Liu Yuan offered to ride north and mobilize the five Xiongnu hosts for Sima Ying.

sentences.zh: 」穎曰：「五部之眾可保發已不？

translations.literal: Ying said, "Can the host of the five sections be guaranteed to mobilize?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying asked, "Can you actually raise those five hosts?

sentences.zh: 縱能發之，鮮卑、烏丸勁速如風雲，何易可當邪？

translations.literal: Even if they can be mobilized, Xianbei and Wuhuan are fierce and swift as wind and cloud—how can they easily be resisted?
translations.idiomatic: Even if you can, Xianbei and Wuhuan move like storms—who stops them once loosed?

sentences.zh: 吾欲奉乘輿還洛陽，避其鋒銳，徐傳檄天下，以逆順制之。

translations.literal: I wish to escort the imperial carriage back to Luoyang, avoid their sharp edge, then slowly transmit summons across All-under-Heaven and control them with obedience and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to escort the throne to Luoyang, dodge their spearpoint, then call the realm to arms on right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 君意何如？

translations.literal: What is your intent?
translations.idiomatic: What do you counsel?

sentences.zh: 」元海曰：「殿下武皇帝之子，有殊勳於王室，威恩光洽，四海欽風，孰不思為殿下沒命投軀者哉，何難發之有乎！

translations.literal: Yuanhai said, "Your Highness is Martial Emperor's son and has extraordinary merit toward the royal house; awe and kindness shine everywhere, and the four seas admire your wind—who would not think to die and cast aside his body for Your Highness—what difficulty is there in mobilizing them!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan answered, "You are Sima Yan's son, beloved across the realm—every warrior would die for you; raising the tribes is no hard task.

sentences.zh: 王浚豎子，東嬴疏屬，豈能與殿下爭衡邪！

translations.literal: Wang Jun is a stripling; Dongying is a distant cousin—how can they match Your Highness!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun is a pup and Sima Teng a cadet branch—neither can rival you.

sentences.zh: 殿下一發鄴宮，示弱於人，洛陽可復至乎？

translations.literal: If Your Highness once leaves the Ye palace, you show weakness to men—can Luoyang be regained?
translations.idiomatic: Flee Ye once and you advertise weakness—will Luoyang ever welcome you back?

sentences.zh: 縱達洛陽，威權不復在殿下也。

translations.literal: Even if you reach Luoyang, awesome authority will no longer be with Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Even in Luoyang you would hold no real power.

sentences.zh: 紙檄尺書，誰為人奉之！

translations.literal: Paper summons an inch long—who will obey them!
translations.idiomatic: Who would heed a sheaf of edicts from a discrowned prince!

sentences.zh: 且東胡之悍不逾五部，願殿下勉撫士眾，靖以鎮之，當為殿下以二部摧東嬴，三部梟王浚，二豎之首可指日而懸矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the eastern Hu are not fiercer than the five sections; I hope Your Highness will encourage and soothe the soldiers and quiet them to hold the city—I will for Your Highness with two sections crush Dongying and with three sections behead Wang Jun; the two striplings' heads can be hung within days.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern tribes are no tougher than our horsemen—stay in Ye, steady the army, and I will smash Sima Teng with two wings and take Wang Jun's head with three; both puppets will swing from the gate in days.

sentences.zh: 」穎悅，拜元海為北單于、參丞相軍事。

translations.literal: Ying was pleased, appointed Yuanhai northern Shanyu, and joined him to the staff of the minister of state.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying cheered up, named Liu Yuan northern Shanyu, and attached him to the chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 元海至左國城，劉宣等上大單于之號，二旬之間，眾已五萬，都于離石。

translations.literal: Yuanhai reached Zuoguocheng; Liu Xuan and others presented the title of great Shanyu; within twenty days the host already numbered fifty thousand, with capital at Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: At Zuoguocheng Liu Xuan proclaimed him great Shanyu; inside twenty days fifty thousand men gathered with capital at Lishi.

sentences.zh: 王浚使將軍祁弘率鮮卑攻鄴，穎敗，挾天子南奔洛陽。

translations.literal: Wang Jun sent General Qi Hong leading Xianbei to attack Ye; Ying was defeated, seized the Son of Heaven, and fled south to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun's general Qi Hong drove Xianbei against Ye; Sima Ying fled south clutching the emperor.

sentences.zh: 元海曰：「穎不用吾言，逆自奔潰，真奴才也。

translations.literal: Yuanhai said, "Ying did not use my words and contrary-wise fled in collapse—he is a true slave.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan sneered, "Sima Ying ignored my counsel and ran—little better than a bondsman.

sentences.zh: 然吾與其有言矣，不可不救。

translations.literal: Yet I had an agreement with him and cannot fail to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Still I promised him aid and must move.

sentences.zh: 」於是命右於陸王劉景、左獨鹿王劉延年等率步騎二萬，將討鮮卑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered King of the Right Yulu Liu Jing, King of the Left Duliu Liu Yannian, and others to lead twenty thousand foot and horse, about to attack the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Liu Jing and Liu Yannian forward with twenty thousand riders—ostensibly against the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 劉宣等固諫曰：「晉為無道，奴隸禦我，是以右賢王猛不勝其忿。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan and others firmly remonstrated, saying, "Jin is without the Way; slaves drive us—therefore the Right Worthy King Meng could not bear his rage.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan blocked him: "Jin treats us like driven slaves—remember how Right Worthy Meng rose in fury.

sentences.zh: 屬晉綱未馳，大事不遂，右賢塗地，單于之恥也。

translations.literal: When Jin's net had not yet slackened, the great matter did not succeed; the Right Worthy was crushed to earth—it was the Shanyu's shame.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's grip was still tight then, and our rising failed—our people's blood is still the Shanyu's shame.

sentences.zh: 今司馬氏父子兄弟自相魚肉，此天厭晉德，授之於我。

translations.literal: Now the Sima father, sons, and brothers devour one another like fish flesh—Heaven tires of Jin's virtue and hands it to us.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Simas devour their own—Heaven has turned from Jin and hands us the mandate.

sentences.zh: 單于積德在躬，為晉人所服，方當興我邦族，復呼韓邪之業，鮮卑、烏丸可以為援，奈何距之而拯仇敵！

translations.literal: The Shanyu has stored virtue in his person and is obeyed by Jin men; you should raise our tribal nation, restore Huhanye's enterprise—Xianbei and Wuhuan can be allies—how turn them away to rescue an enemy!
translations.idiomatic: You already command Jin's awe; rebuild our nation and Huhanye's glory—use the steppe peoples, do not waste your strength saving a foe.

sentences.zh: 今天假手於我，不可違也。

translations.literal: Now Heaven lends its hand to us—it cannot be disobeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven lends us this chance—we dare not refuse.

sentences.zh: 違天不祥，逆眾不濟；

translations.literal: To disobey Heaven is inauspicious; to oppose the multitude will not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Defy Heaven and fortune flees; defy your warriors and nothing succeeds;

sentences.zh: 天與不取，反受其咎。

translations.literal: Heaven gives and you do not take—instead you receive its blame.
translations.idiomatic: Reject Heaven's gift and you earn its curse.

sentences.zh: 願單于勿疑。

translations.literal: I beg the Shanyu not to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Do not hesitate, Shanyu.

sentences.zh: 」元海曰：「善。

translations.literal: Yuanhai said, "Good.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan said, "Well spoken.

sentences.zh: 當為崇岡峻阜，何能為培塿乎！

translations.literal: We ought to be high ridges and steep mounds—how can we be mere hillocks!
translations.idiomatic: We aim to be mountain ranges, not molehills.

sentences.zh: 夫帝王豈有常哉，大禹出於西戎，文王生於東夷，顧惟德所授耳。

translations.literal: For emperors and kings—how can there be constancy? Great Yu came from the western Rong; King Wen was born among the eastern Yi—it depends only on whom virtue invests.
translations.idiomatic: Thrones never stay fixed: Yu rose from western tribes, Wen from eastern barbarians—virtue alone decides who rules.

sentences.zh: 今見眾十餘萬，皆一當晉十，鼓行而摧亂晉，猶拉枯耳。

translations.literal: Now I see a host of over a hundred thousand, each one worth ten Jin soldiers; beating the drum and advancing to crush chaotic Jin is like snapping dead wood.
translations.idiomatic: I command a hundred thousand, each man worth ten Jin soldiers; marching on Luoyang will splinter them like dry twigs.

sentences.zh: 上可成漢高之業，下不失為魏氏。

translations.literal: Above I can complete Gaozu's enterprise; below I will not fall short of the house of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Best case I match Han Gaozu; worst I still rival Cao Wei.

sentences.zh: 雖然，晉人未必同我。

translations.literal: Even so, Jin men will not necessarily join me.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jin subjects may not flock to us.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下世長，恩德結于人心，是以昭烈崎嶇於一州之地，而能抗衡於天下。

translations.literal: Han possessed the realm for generations long; kindness and virtue knotted in human hearts; therefore Zhaolie, twisted on one province's ground, could yet resist All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruled long enough that the people still love its memory—Liu Bei clung to one province yet defied the world.

sentences.zh: 吾又漢氏之甥，約為兄弟，兄亡弟紹，不亦可乎？

translations.literal: I am moreover Han's nephew by marriage, covenanted as brothers; the elder died and the younger continues—is that not fitting?
translations.idiomatic: We are sworn brothers to the Liu house; when the elder line fell should not the younger inherit?

sentences.zh: 且可稱漢，追尊後主，以懷人望。

translations.literal: Moreover one may style the state Han, posthumously honour the last lord, and thereby embrace human hope.
translations.idiomatic: Call our state Han, enshrine the last Han emperor, and the hearts of the people will follow.

sentences.zh: 」乃遷于左國城，遠人歸附者數萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved to Zuoguocheng, and distant people who attached numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted to Zuoguocheng and tens of thousands of far wanderers joined him.

sentences.zh: 永興元年，元海乃為壇於南郊，僭即漢王位，下令曰：「昔我太祖高皇帝以神武應期，廓開大業。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxing Yuanhai then built an altar south of the suburbs and usurped accession as King of Han, ordering, "Formerly our Grand Progenitor the High Emperor, by divine martialness answered the period and opened the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxing year one Liu Yuan built a suburban altar and proclaimed himself King of Han, intoning how Han Gaozu founded the dynasty by divine war.

sentences.zh: 太宗孝文皇帝重以明德，升平漢道。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor, Emperor Wen of Filial Piety, again by bright virtue elevated the Han Way to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi lifted the realm with pure virtue.

sentences.zh: 世宗孝武皇帝拓土攘夷，地過唐日。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Filial Piety, Shizong, expanded the soil and pushed the Yi; the land passed Tang days.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi widened the map beyond even Tang's reach.

sentences.zh: 中宗孝宣皇帝搜揚俊乂，多士盈朝。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Filial Piety, Zhongzong, searched out and raised the excellent, so that many shi filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xuandi filled court with talent he sought out.

sentences.zh: 是我祖宗道邁三王，功高五帝，故卜年倍于夏商，卜世過於姬氏。

translations.literal: Thus our forefathers' Way overtook the Three Kings and merit topped the Five Thearchs; therefore the divined years doubled Xia and Shang, and the divined generations surpassed the Ji clan.
translations.idiomatic: So Han virtue outshone the Three Kings and merit topped the Five Thearchs—its allotted years doubled Xia and Shang, its generations outlasted Zhou.

sentences.zh: 而元成多僻，哀平短祚，賊臣王莽，滔天篡逆。

translations.literal: Yet Yuancheng were many depraved, Ai and Ping had short fates, and the traitorous minister Wang Mang swelled to heaven and usurped in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Later emperors slipped; Ai and Ping died young; Wang Mang usurped the throne.

sentences.zh: 我世祖光武皇帝誕資聖武，恢復鴻基，祀漢配天，不失舊物，俾三光晦而復明，神器幽而復顯。

translations.literal: Our Shizu, Emperor Guangwu of the Han, was born with sacred martialness, restored the great foundation, sacrificed to Han and matched Heaven, not losing old tokens, so that the three luminaries, having darkened, again brightened, and the divine vessel, having been hidden, again appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu restored Han, realigned heaven and earth, and brought back the sun, moon, and stars.

sentences.zh: 顯宗孝明皇帝、肅宗孝章皇帝累葉重暉，炎光再闡。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Filial Piety, Xianzong, and Emperor Zhang of Filial Piety, Suzong, piled generation on generation of doubled radiance, and the fiery light again blazed.
translations.idiomatic: Ming and Zhang emperors relit Han's fire generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 自和安已後，皇綱漸頹，天步艱難，國統頻絕。

translations.literal: From He and An onward the imperial net gradually collapsed, heaven's step was hard, and the state's thread repeatedly broke.
translations.idiomatic: After He and An the dynasty frayed, heaven's course faltered, and the succession snapped again and again.

sentences.zh: 黃巾海沸於九州，群閹毒流于四海，董卓因之肆其猖勃，曹操父子凶逆相尋。

translations.literal: Yellow Turbans seethed like sea foam in the Nine Provinces; packs of eunuchs poisoned the four seas; Dong Zhuo thereupon let loose his raging arrogance; Cao Cao father and son followed each other in vicious rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Turbans boiled across the nine regions, eunuchs poisoned every quarter, Dong Zhuo ran wild, and the Caos seized power in turn.

sentences.zh: 故孝湣委棄萬國，昭烈播越岷蜀，冀否終有泰，旋軫舊京。

translations.literal: Therefore Xiaomin cast aside the myriad states, and Zhaolie wandered Min and Shu, hoping that the bad end would have a good turn and the capital could be turned again.
translations.idiomatic: Han emperors fled the realm; Liu Bei held Shu, hoping fate would turn and Luoyang return.

sentences.zh: 何圖天未悔禍，後帝窘辱。

translations.literal: Who could have thought Heaven had not yet repented the disaster, and the later emperor met shame and insult.
translations.idiomatic: Yet heaven still refused mercy and the last Han child met humiliation.

sentences.zh: 自社稷淪喪，宗廟之不血食四十年於茲矣。

translations.literal: From the altars' ruin and loss, the ancestral temples have gone without blood sacrifice for forty years to this point.
translations.idiomatic: Forty years now the Han shrines have gone hungry.

sentences.zh: 今天誘其衷，悔禍皇漢，使司馬氏父子兄弟迭相殘滅。

translations.literal: Now Heaven opens their bosoms, repents the disaster toward august Han, and makes the Sima father, sons, and brothers destroy one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Now heaven stirs pity, repents toward Han, and sets the Simas at one another's throats.

sentences.zh: 黎庶塗炭，靡所控告。

translations.literal: The black-haired people are smeared in mud and charcoal, with nowhere to cry their complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The common folk burn in mud and ash with no court to hear them.

sentences.zh: 孤今猥為群公所推，紹修三祖之業。

translations.literal: I, alone, am now vulgarly pushed by the host of dukes to continue and repair the enterprise of the three ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: I am pressed by you lords to renew the work of Han's three founders.

sentences.zh: 顧茲尪暗，戰惶靡厝。

translations.literal: Looking at this dim dullness, I tremble and have no place to put myself.
translations.idiomatic: I am small and weak and tremble at the charge.

sentences.zh: 但以大恥未雪，社稷無主，銜膽棲冰，勉從群議。

translations.literal: Yet because the great shame is not yet washed away and the altars lack a master, holding gall and dwelling on ice, I reluctantly follow the host's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the great shame stands unavenged and the throne is empty—so I swallow bile and accept.

sentences.zh: 」乃赦其境內，年號元熙，追尊劉禪為孝懷皇帝，立漢高祖以下三祖五宗神主而祭之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he amnestied his territory, took the era-name Yuanci, posthumously honoured Liu Shan as Emperor Xiaohuai, and set up spirit tablets for Han Gaozu down through the three ancestors and five temples and sacrificed to them.
translations.idiomatic: He declared amnesty, era Yuanci, honoured Liu Shan posthumously, and set tablets for Han's ancestors through five generations.

sentences.zh: 立其妻呼延氏為王后。

translations.literal: He established his wife Lady Huyan as queen.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lady Huyan queen.

sentences.zh: 置百官，以劉宣為丞相，崔游為御史大夫，劉宏為太尉，其餘拜授各有差。

translations.literal: He set up the hundred offices, making Liu Xuan chancellor, Cui You imperial counsellor, Liu Hong grand commandant, and the rest received appointments each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a government: Liu Xuan chancellor, Cui You censor-in-chief, Liu Hong grand commandant, and the rest ranked by merit.

sentences.zh: 東嬴公騰使將軍聶玄討之，戰於大陵，玄師敗績，騰懼，率并州二萬餘戶下山東，遂所在為寇。

translations.literal: Dongying Duke Teng sent General Nie Xuan to attack him; they fought at Daling; Xuan's army was routed; Teng, in fear, led more than twenty thousand households of Bingzhou down to Shandong, and thereupon everywhere became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng sent Nie Xuan against him, lost at Daling, then fled Bing with twenty thousand families eastward, leaving the province to chaos.

sentences.zh: 元海遣其建武將軍劉曜寇太原、泫氏、屯留、長子、中都，皆陷之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai sent his General Who Establishes Might Liu Yao to raid Taiyuan, Xuan, Tunliu, Changzi, and Zhongdu—all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan sent Liu Yao to storm Taiyuan, Xuan, Tunliu, Changzi, and Zhongdu—all fell.

sentences.zh: 二年，騰又遣司馬瑜、周良、石鮮等討之，次於離石汾城。

translations.literal: In the second year Teng again sent Sima Yu, Zhou Liang, Shi Xian, and others to attack him, halting at Fencheng of Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Sima Teng sent Sima Yu, Zhou Liang, and Shi Xian to Lishi's Fencheng.

sentences.zh: 元海遣其武牙將軍劉欽等六軍距瑜等，四戰，瑜皆敗，欽振旅而歸。

translations.literal: Yuanhai sent his General Who Martial Fangs Liu Qin and six armies to oppose Yu and the others; after four battles Yu was defeated each time, and Qin returned with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan sent Liu Qin with six hosts; after four battles Jin fled and Liu Qin marched home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 是歲，離石大饑，遷于黎亭，以就邸閣穀，留其太尉劉宏、護軍馬景守離石，使大司農卜豫運糧以給之。

translations.literal: That year Lishi suffered great famine; they moved to Liting to draw on granary grain, leaving Grand Commandant Liu Hong and Protector Ma Jing to guard Lishi, and ordered Grand Minister of Agriculture Bu Yu to transport grain to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck Lishi, so the court moved to Liting granaries while Liu Hong and Ma Jing held Lishi and Bu Yu shipped grain.

sentences.zh: 以其前將軍劉景為使持節、征討大都督、大將軍，要擊并州刺史劉琨于版橋，為琨所敗，琨遂據晉陽。

translations.literal: He made his former general Liu Jing credential-holder, grand commander for conquest, grand general, and intercepted Bing Governor Liu Kun at Banqiao; he was defeated by Kun, and Kun thereupon occupied Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Jing to ambush Liu Kun at Banqiao; Liu Kun crushed him and took Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 其侍中劉殷、王育進諫元海曰：「殿下自起兵以來，漸已一周，而顓守偏方，王威未震。

translations.literal: His attendants Liu Yin and Wang Yu advanced remonstrance to Yuanhai, saying, "Since Your Highness raised troops it has gradually been a full cycle, yet you only hold a corner; kingly awe has not yet shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin and Wang Yu urged him: "A year has passed and you still hug one corner—your majesty has not yet thundered abroad.

sentences.zh: 誠能命將四出，決機一擲，梟劉琨，定河東，建帝號，鼓行而南，克長安而都之，以關中之眾席捲洛陽，如指掌耳。

translations.literal: If you truly can order generals to go out on four sides, cast the die once, behead Liu Kun, settle Hedong, establish an imperial title, beat the drum southward, take Chang'an as capital, then with the hosts of Guanzhong roll up Luoyang—it is like turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Send four columns, kill Liu Kun, secure Hedong, proclaim the throne, march on Chang'an, then sweep from the passes to Luoyang like turning your hand.

sentences.zh: 此高皇帝之所以創啟鴻基，克殄強楚者也。

translations.literal: This is how the High Emperor opened the great foundation and utterly destroyed mighty Chu.
translations.idiomatic: That was Gaozu's road to crush Chu.

sentences.zh: 」元海悅曰：「此孤心也。

translations.literal: Yuanhai, pleased, said, "This is Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan cried, "That is my own mind too.

sentences.zh: 」遂進據河東，攻寇蒲阪、平陽，皆陷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced and occupied Hedong, attacked and raided Puyin and Pingyang, and both fell.
translations.idiomatic: He drove into Hedong, stormed Puyin and Pingyang, and took both.

sentences.zh: 元海遂入都蒲子，河東、平陽屬縣壘壁盡降。

translations.literal: Yuanhai thereupon entered and made his capital at Puzi; fortified camps of the counties of Hedong and Pingyang all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He moved the capital to Puzi; every fort in Hedong and Pingyang opened its gates.

sentences.zh: 時汲桑起兵趙魏，上郡四部鮮卑陸逐延、氏酋大單于征、東萊王彌及石勒等並相次降之，元海悉署其官爵。

translations.literal: At that time Ji Sang raised troops in Zhao and Wei; Lüzhuyan of the four Xianbei sections of Shangjun, Di chief Great-Shanyu Zheng, Wang Mi of Donglai, and Shi Le in succession each surrendered to him; Yuanhai all appointed their offices and noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang rose in Zhao-Wei; Xianbei, Di, Wang Mi, and Shi Le came over in turn; Liu Yuan handed each a title.

sentences.zh: ，元海僭即皇帝位，大赦境內，改元永鳳。

translations.literal: , Yuanhai usurped the imperial throne, greatly amnestied his territory, and changed the era to Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Yuan declared himself emperor, amnestied the realm, and took the era name Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 以其大將軍劉和為大司馬，封梁王，尚書令劉歡樂為大司徒，封陳留王，御史大夫呼延翼為大司空，封雁州郡公，宗室以親疏為等，悉封郡縣王，異姓以勳謀為差，皆封郡縣公侯。

translations.literal: He made his grand general Liu He grand marshal and Prince of Liang, Director in the Masters of Writing Liu Huanle grand minister of education and Prince of Chenliu, Imperial Counsellor Huyan Yi grand minister of works and Duke of Yanzhou commandery, enfeoffed the imperial clan by closeness and distance each as commandery or county princes, and enfeoffed those of other surnames by merit and stratagem each as commandery or county dukes, marquises, or lords.
translations.idiomatic: He named Liu He grand marshal and prince of Liang, Liu Huanle grand tutor and prince of Chenliu, Huyan Yi grand minister of works, ennobled kinsmen by degree of kin, and outsiders by merit.

sentences.zh: 太史令宣于修之言於元海曰：「陛下雖龍興鳳翔。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Xianyu Xiuzhi spoke to Yuanhai, saying, "Although Your Majesty has risen like dragon and phoenix,
translations.idiomatic: The court astrologer Xianyu Xiuzhi said, "Though you rise like dragon and phoenix,

sentences.zh: 奄受大命，然遺晉未殄，皇居仄陋，紫宮之變，猶鐘晉氏，不出三年，必克洛陽。

translations.literal: and suddenly received the great mandate, yet the remnant Jin is not yet exterminated, the imperial residence is narrow and mean, and the Purple Palace's portents still toll for the Jin house; within three years Luoyang will surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Jin still lives, your capital is mean, and the stars still beat for Luoyang—within three years Jin's capital falls.

sentences.zh: 薄子崎嶇，非可久安。

translations.literal: Puzi is rugged and is not a place for long peace.
translations.idiomatic: Puzi is too broken for a lasting throne.

sentences.zh: 平陽勢有紫氣，兼陶唐舊都，願陛下上迎乾象，下協坤祥。

translations.literal: Pingyang's aspect has purple vapour and moreover is the old capital of Yao of Tao Tang; I hope Your Majesty will above welcome the Qian image and below harmonize with Kun's auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang shows purple mist and was Yao's ancient seat—move there to match heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 」於是遷都平陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon they moved the capital to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court therefore shifted the capital to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 汾水中得玉璽，文曰「有新保之」，蓋王莽時璽也。

translations.literal: In the Fen River they obtained a jade seal whose inscription read 'You have Xin to preserve it'—it was the seal of Wang Mang's time.
translations.idiomatic: Dredging the Fen yielded a jade seal inscribed for Wang Mang's usurpation—words promising a new protector.

sentences.zh: 得者因增「泉海光」三字，元海以為己瑞，大赦境內，改年河瑞。

translations.literal: The finder therefore added the three characters 'Spring Sea Radiance'; Yuanhai took it as an omen for himself, greatly amnestied his territory, and changed the year to Herui.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers carved three lucky words onto it; Liu Yuan read it as his own omen, declared amnesty, and renamed the era Herui.

sentences.zh: 封子裕為齊王，隆為魯王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed his son Yu as Prince of Qi and Long as Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He named Liu Yu prince of Qi and Liu Long prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 於是命其子聰與王彌進寇洛陽，劉曜與趙固等為之後繼。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered his son Cong and Wang Mi to advance and raid Luoyang, with Liu Yao and Zhao Gu and others as their rear support.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Liu Cong and Wang Mi against Luoyang while Liu Yao and Zhao Gu followed in support.

sentences.zh: 東海王越遣平北將軍曹武、將軍宋抽、彭默等距之，王師敗績。

translations.literal: Prince Sima Yue of Donghai sent General Who Pacifies the North Cao Wu and generals Song Chou, Peng Mo, and others to oppose them; the royal army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue answered with Cao Wu, Song Chou, and Peng Mo—and lost.

sentences.zh: 聰等長驅至宜陽，平昌公模遣將軍淳于定、呂毅等自長安討之，戰于宜陽，定等敗績。

translations.literal: Cong and the others drove straight to Yiyang; Duke of Pingchang Sima Mo sent generals Chunyu Ding and Lü Yi and others from Chang'an to attack them; they fought at Yiyang, and Ding and the others were routed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong raced to Yiyang until Sima Mo's generals Chunyu Ding and Lü Yi struck from Chang'an; Jin still lost at Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 聰恃連勝，不設備，弘農太守垣延詐降。

translations.literal: Cong, relying on successive victories, set no precautions; Governor of Hongnong Yuan Yan feigned surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong, drunk on wins, let his guard down; Governor Yuan Yan of Hongnong faked defection.

sentences.zh: 夜襲，聰軍大敗而還，元海素服迎師。

translations.literal: He night-attacked; Cong's army was greatly defeated and returned; Yuanhai in plain garb welcomed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yan raided by night and shattered Liu Cong's column; Liu Yuan met the beaten army in mourning white.

sentences.zh: 是冬，復大發卒，遣聰、彌與劉曜、劉景等率精騎五萬寇洛陽，使呼延翼率步卒繼之，敗王師于河南。

translations.literal: That winter he again greatly issued soldiers, sending Cong, Mi, Liu Yao, Liu Jing, and others to lead fifty thousand picked cavalry to raid Luoyang, ordered Huyan Yi to lead foot soldiers after them, and defeated the royal army south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Winter brought a second offensive: fifty thousand horse under Liu Cong, Liu Yao, and Liu Jing, foot under Huyan Yi, crushing Jin south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 聰進屯於西明門，護軍賈胤夜薄之，戰于大夏門，斬聰將呼延顥，其眾遂潰。

translations.literal: Cong advanced and camped at the Ximing Gate; Protector Jia Yin attacked them by night; they fought at the Daxia Gate, beheaded Cong's general Huyan Hao, and their host thereupon broke.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong reached the western bright gate until Jia Yin struck by night at Daxia Gate, killed Huyan Hao, and scattered the Han van.

sentences.zh: 聰回軍而南。

translations.literal: Cong turned the army southward.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong drew his host south.

sentences.zh: 壁于洛水，尋進屯宣陽門，曜屯上東門，彌屯廣陽門，景攻大夏門，聰親祈嵩嶽，令其將劉厲、呼延朗等督留軍。

translations.literal: They walled at the Luo River, then advanced to camp at the Xuanyang Gate; Yao camped at the Upper East Gate, Mi at the Guangyang Gate, Jing attacked the Daxia Gate; Cong personally prayed at Mount Song, ordering his generals Liu Li, Huyan Lang, and others to supervise the remaining army.
translations.idiomatic: They bridged the Luo, ringed Xuanyang, Upper East, and Guangyang gates, while Liu Cong climbed Songshan to pray and left Liu Li and Huyan Lang holding the rear.

sentences.zh: 東海王越命參軍孫詢、將軍丘光、樓裒等率帳下勁卒三千，自宣陽門擊朗，斬之。

translations.literal: Prince Sima Yue of Donghai ordered staffer Sun Xun and generals Qiu Guang, Lou Pou, and others to lead three thousand picked troops of the headquarters from the Xuanyang Gate to strike Lang and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue sent Sun Xun, Qiu Guang, and Lou Pou with three thousand elites out Xuanyang Gate to kill Huyan Lang.

sentences.zh: 聰聞而馳還。

translations.literal: When Cong heard it he galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong galloped back to save his line.

sentences.zh: 厲懼聰之罪己也，赴水而死。

translations.literal: Li, fearing Cong would blame him, threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Liu Cong's wrath, Liu Li drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 王彌謂聰曰：「今既失利，洛陽猶固，殿下不如還師，徐為後舉。

translations.literal: Wang Mi said to Cong, "Now that we have already lost advantage, Luoyang is still solid; Your Highness had better return the army and plan later action.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi urged Liu Cong, "Luoyang still holds; pull back and strike another day.

sentences.zh: 下官當於袞豫之間收兵積穀，伏聽嚴期。

translations.literal: This humble official will between Yan and Yu gather troops and store grain, and await your stern date.
translations.idiomatic: I will recruit between Yan and Yu and wait your signal.

sentences.zh: 」宣于修之又言於元海曰：「歲在辛未，當得洛陽。

translations.literal: Xianyu Xiuzhi again spoke to Yuanhai, saying, "The year being xinwei, Luoyang should be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Xiuzhi added, "The almanac says xinwei year takes Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 今晉氣猶盛，大軍不歸，必敗。

translations.literal: Now Jin's vapour is still strong; if the great army does not return, it will certainly be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's star still burns bright—linger and you will lose.

sentences.zh: 」元海馳遣黃門郎傅詢召聰等還師。

translations.literal: Yuanhai galloped sending Gentleman at the Yellow Gates Fu Xun to summon Cong and the others to return the army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan sent Fu Xun riding night and day to recall Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 王彌出自轘轅，越遣薄盛等追擊彌，戰於新汲，彌師敗績。

translations.literal: Wang Mi exited Huanyuan; Yue sent Bo Sheng and others to pursue and attack Mi; they fought at Xinji, and Mi's army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi slipped through Huanyuan; Sima Yue's Bo Sheng ran him down at Xinji and broke his column.

sentences.zh: 於是攝薄阪之戍，還於平陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon they drew in the garrison at Boban and returned to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Han troops lifted the Boban screen and marched back to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 以劉歡樂為太傅，劉聰為大司徒，劉延年為大司空，劉洋為大司馬，赦其境內。

translations.literal: He made Liu Huanle grand tutor, Liu Cong grand minister of education, Liu Yannian grand minister of works, Liu Yang grand marshal, amnestied his territory.
translations.idiomatic: He named Liu Huanle grand tutor, Liu Cong minister of education, Liu Yannian minister of works, Liu Yang grand marshal, and amnestied the realm.

sentences.zh: 立其妻單氏為皇后，子和為皇太子，封子乂為北海王。

translations.literal: He established his wife Lady Shan as empress, Liu He as imperial heir, and enfeoffed his son Yi as Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: He crowned Lady Shan empress, named Liu He crown prince, and made Liu Yi prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 元海寢疾，將為顧托之計，以歡樂為太宰，洋為太傅，延年為太保，聰為大司馬、大單于，並錄尚書事，置單于台于平陽西，以其子裕為大司徒。

translations.literal: Yuanhai lay ill and planned for testamentary charge; he made Huanle grand steward, Yang grand tutor, Yannian grand protector, Cong grand marshal and great Shanyu, all jointly recording Masters of Writing affairs, set up the Shanyu terrace west of Pingyang, and made his son Yu grand minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing death, Liu Yuan named Liu Huanle grand steward, Liu Yang grand tutor, Liu Yannian grand protector, and Liu Cong both grand marshal and great Shanyu with authority over the Masters of Writing; he built a Shanyu platform west of Pingyang and kept Liu Yu as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 元海疾篤，召歡樂及洋等人禁中受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: Yuanhai's illness became grave; he summoned Huanle and Yang and others into the palace to receive testament ordering them to assist the government.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he called Liu Huanle, Liu Yang, and others inside to take regency oaths.

sentences.zh: 以永嘉四年死，在位六年，偽諡光文皇帝，廟號高祖，墓號永光陵。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Yongjia, having been on the throne six years; his false posthumous title was Emperor Guangwen, temple name Gaozu, tomb name Yongguangling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yongjia four after six years on the throne, posthumously styled Emperor Guangwen, temple Gaozu, tomb Yongguang.

sentences.zh: 子和立。

translations.literal: He succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He succeeded.

translations.literal: The transmitted line consists of an equals sign with no lexical gloss in the edition used here.
translations.idiomatic: The edition inserts a lone equals sign between biographical sections.

sentences.zh: 子 劉和

translations.literal: Son Liu He
translations.idiomatic: Liu He

sentences.zh: =和字玄泰。

translations.literal: He, style Xuantai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He, courtesy name Xuantai—the leading mark is an edition artifact.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，雄毅美姿儀，好學夙成，習《毛詩》、《左氏春秋》、《鄭氏易》。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi tall; he was fierce, resolute, and handsome in bearing; he loved study and matured early, studying Mao's Odes, Zuo's Spring and Autumn, and Zheng's Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet, stern and handsome, read deeply from boyhood in the Mao Odes, Zuo commentary, and Zheng Xuan's *Changes*.

sentences.zh: 及為儲貳，內多猜忌，馭下無恩。

translations.literal: When he became heir apparent, inwardly he was much suspicious and jealous, and in ruling subordinates lacked kindness.
translations.idiomatic: As crown prince he grew paranoid and harsh toward his staff.

sentences.zh: 元海死，和嗣偽位。

translations.literal: When Yuanhai died, He succeeded to the false throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan died Liu He took the Han throne.

sentences.zh: 其衛尉西昌王劉銳、宗正呼延攸恨不參顧命也，說和曰：「先帝不惟輕重之計，而使三王總強兵于內，大司馬握十萬勁卒居於近郊，陛下今便為寄坐耳。

translations.literal: His Commandant of the Guards Liu Rui of Xichang and Director of the Imperial Clan Huyan You resented not being included in the testamentary charge, and counselled He, saying, "The former emperor did not weigh the balance of power but let three kings command strong troops inside, while the grand marshal grasps a hundred thousand crack troops near the suburbs; Your Majesty from this morning is merely a guest on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Liu Rui and Huyan You, bitter at being left out of the regency, warned Liu He: "Your father left three royal brothers garrisoned inside the capital while Liu Cong holds a hundred thousand veterans just outside—you sit the throne as a mere lodger.

sentences.zh: 此之禍難，未可測也，顧陛下早為之所。

translations.literal: This misfortune cannot be fathomed; I hope Your Majesty will early deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: No one can say how this ends—move against them now.

sentences.zh: 」和即攸之甥也，深然之，召其領軍劉盛及劉欽、馬景等告之。

translations.literal: He was immediately You's nephew and deeply approved, summoning his Army Commander Liu Sheng and Liu Qin, Ma Jing, and others to inform them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He, You's nephew, agreed and called Liu Sheng, Liu Qin, and Ma Jing to the plot.

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「先帝尚在殯宮，四王未有逆節，今忽一旦自相魚肉，臣恐人不食陛下之余。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "The former emperor is still in the mourning palace; the four kings have shown no treason; if now suddenly flesh and blood devour one another, your servant fears men will not eat Your Majesty's leftovers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng protested: "Your father still lies in state and your brothers show no treason—turn on them now and the world will spit your leavings.

sentences.zh: 四海未定，大業甫爾，願陛下以上成先帝鴻基為志，且塞耳勿聽此狂簡之言也。

translations.literal: The four seas are not yet settled, the great enterprise has barely begun; I hope Your Majesty will take completing the former emperor's great foundation as your aim, and for the moment stop your ears and do not listen to these mad and rash words.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still raw; honour your father's work and deafen yourself to wild counsel.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：'豈無他人，不如我同父。

translations.literal: The Odes says, 'Is it that I have no others—not like my same father.'
translations.idiomatic: The *Classic of Poetry* asks, is there no one else as close as a brother?

sentences.zh: '陛下既不信諸弟，復誰可信哉！

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty already does not trust the various younger brothers, whom again can you trust!
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot trust brothers, whom can you trust?

sentences.zh: 」銳、攸怒曰：「今日之議，理無有二。

translations.literal: Rui and You angrily said, "Today's deliberation allows no second principle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rui and Huyan You snarled, "This council brooks no dissent.

sentences.zh: 」於是命左右刃之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered those at his left and right to blade them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He ordered guards to cut them down.

sentences.zh: 景懼曰：「惟陛下詔，臣等以死奉之，蔑不濟矣。

translations.literal: Jing, in fear, said, "Only await Your Majesty's edict; your servants will follow unto death—nothing will then fail.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jing stammered obedience: "Command us and we die in the attempt."

sentences.zh: 」乃相與盟於東堂，使銳、景攻聰，攸率劉安國攻裕，使侍中劉乘、武衛劉欽攻魯王隆，尚書田密、武衛劉璿攻北海王乂。

translations.literal: Thereupon they mutually covenanted in the eastern hall, sending Rui and Jing to attack Cong, You leading Liu Anguo to attack Yu, ordering Palace Attendant Liu Cheng and Martial Guard Liu Qin to attack Prince of Lu Long, Masters of Writing Tian Mi and Martial Guard Liu Xuan to attack Prince of Beihai Yi.
translations.idiomatic: They swore in the eastern hall: Liu Rui and Ma Jing would strike Liu Cong; Huyan You and Liu Anguo would hit Liu Yu; Liu Cheng and Liu Qin would move on Liu Long; Tian Mi and Liu Xuan would storm Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 密、璿等使人斬關奔於聰，聰命貫甲以待之。

translations.literal: Tian Mi, Liu Xuan, and others sent men to cut the pass bars and flee to Cong; Cong ordered armour donned to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Mi and Liu Xuan broke out to warn Liu Cong, who ordered his men under arms.

sentences.zh: 銳知聰之有備也，馳還，與攸、乘等會攻隆、裕。

translations.literal: Rui knew Cong had preparations and galloped back, joining You and Cheng to attack Long and Yu together.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rui saw the trap, wheeled back, and with Huyan You and Liu Cheng struck Liu Long and Liu Yu instead.

sentences.zh: 攸、乘懼安國、欽之有異志也，斬之。

translations.literal: You and Cheng feared Anguo and Qin harboured different intent and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan You and Liu Cheng killed Liu Anguo and Liu Qin, fearing betrayal.

sentences.zh: 是日，斬裕及隆。

translations.literal: That day they beheaded Yu and Long.
translations.idiomatic: That day Liu Yu and Liu Long died.

sentences.zh: 聰攻西明門，克之。

translations.literal: Cong attacked the Ximing Gate and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong stormed the western bright gate.

sentences.zh: 銳等奔入南宮，前鋒隨之，斬和於光極西室。

translations.literal: Rui and the others fled into the southern palace; the vanguard followed and beheaded He in the western chamber of Guangji.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers cornered Liu Rui in the southern palace and slew Liu He in the Guangji west hall.

sentences.zh: 銳、攸梟首通衢。

translations.literal: Rui and You had their heads hung on the thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rui and Huyan You's heads went to the public crossroads.

sentences.zh: 劉宣

translations.literal: Liu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan

sentences.zh: 劉宣，字士則。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan, style Shize.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, courtesy name Shize.

sentences.zh: 朴鈍少言，好學修潔。

translations.literal: He was plain, dull, and sparing of speech, loved study and cultivated purity.
translations.idiomatic: He was quiet, plain-spoken, bookish, and scrupulously clean.

sentences.zh: 師事樂安孫炎，沈精積思，不舍晝夜，好《毛詩》、《左氏傳》。

translations.literal: He took as teacher Sun Yan of Le'an, sinking his essence and piling thought, not quitting day or night, loving Mao's Odes and Zuo's Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Sun Yan of Le'an with obsessive focus, loving the Mao Odes and Zuo commentary.

sentences.zh: 炎每歎之曰：「宣若遇漢武，當逾于金日磾也。

translations.literal: Yan always sighed of him, saying, "If Xuan had met Han Wudi, he would have surpassed Jin Midi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yan sighed that under Han Wudi he would have outshone Jin Midi.

sentences.zh: 」學成而返，不出門閭蓋數年。

translations.literal: When study was completed he returned, not going out his gate for several years.
translations.idiomatic: When his course finished he stayed home for years without stepping past his gate.

sentences.zh: 每讀《漢書》，至《蕭何》、《鄧禹傳》，未曾不反覆詠之，曰：「大丈夫若遭二祖，終不令二公獨擅美於前矣。

translations.literal: Whenever he read the Han Documents, reaching the treatises on Xiao He and Deng Yu, he never failed repeatedly to intone them, saying, "If a great husband met the two Founders, in the end he would not let the two dukes alone monopolize beauty before them.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the *Book of Han* chapters on Xiao He and Deng Yu he would chant, "Had I served Han's founders I would not leave those two alone the laurels.

sentences.zh: 」并州刺史王廣言之于武帝，帝召見，嘉其占對，因曰：「吾未見宣，謂廣言虛耳。

translations.literal: The Governor of Bing, Wang Guang, spoke of him to Emperor Wu; the Emperor summoned and saw him, praised his answers, and therefore said, "We had not yet seen Xuan and thought Guang's words empty.
translations.idiomatic: Bing governor Wang Guang praised him to Sima Yan, who interviewed Liu Xuan and said, "I thought Wang Guang exaggerated.

sentences.zh: 今見其進止風儀，真所謂如圭如璋，觀其性質，足能撫集本部。

translations.literal: Now seeing his advance and retreat, wind and bearing, he is truly called like jade, like fine jade; observing his nature and substance, he is sufficient to soothe and gather his native command.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his carriage I know the proverb 'like jade tablets'—he can truly pacify his people.

sentences.zh: 」乃以宣為右部都督，特給赤幛曲蓋。

translations.literal: Thereupon he made Xuan commander of the right section, specially granting red pennant and curved canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan named him right-section commander with crimson pennant and curved awning.

sentences.zh: 蒞官清恪，所部懷之。

translations.literal: When he took office he was pure and scrupulous; those under his command cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed cleanly and his tribes loved him.

sentences.zh: 元海即王位，宣之謀也，故特荷尊重，勳戚莫二，軍國內外靡不專之。

translations.literal: When Yuanhai assumed the kingly title it was Xuan's stratagem; therefore he alone bore utmost respect; among meritorious kin there was no second; none within or without the army and state did not defer to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan's kingship was Liu Xuan's design, so he alone enjoyed supreme trust—no kinsman or minister rivalled his authority.
